meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided on the zero.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Nobody called me, and Owen found out on his phone in the middle of class. What do you have?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Students misremember lines all the time, Hale. A bad quotation is not proof of anything. Show me the page, and show me how you checked it.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. I'm writing that down, and the principal will be reading it tonight.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, a written apology, and confirmation that nothing is on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology and a promise that nothing goes on Owen's record, so that is not the fair outcome, which was a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, and it was your END MEETING that closed it, not her clock.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before you called her, in one plain sentence, and she gave you a flat okay because it answered her complaint about procedure.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it runs in the family, which attacked her children instead of showing her anything, and it sent her straight back to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was a quoted line missing from the play, with no times or late nights, so it never got near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked you to show the page and how you checked, put the essay page next to the play's text so she could verify the missing line herself, before saying anything else about Owen's family.
